newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Britain's Hannay due in Cyprus before peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Hannay due in Cyprus before peace talks.

text.p: Britain's special representative on the Cyprus conflict, Sir David Hannay, is due in Cyprus in June for talks with leaders of the two communities before direct talks between them, a British spokesman said on Wednesday.
The spokesman for the British High Commission told Reuters it was too early to be specific about issues to be discussed.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is expected to invite the leader of the Greek Cypriot community, President Glafcos Clerides, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash to direct talks at the end of June. It would be their first encounter for nearly three years.
Greek and Turkish Cypriots have been living apart since Turkey invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military junta ruling Greece at the time.
Greece, Turkey and Britain are guarantor powers of Cyprus under agreements granting the former British colony independence in 1960.

The United Nations hopes a resumption of stalled peace talks could pave the way for a comprehensive settlement of the conflict now splitting the island, a feat that a small army of U.N. and international mediators have failed to accomplish for more than two decades.
